title: Threshold registry — threshold-contract SoT shape (TRK-339 WS1a / #1200 D2)
description: Shape contract for rule-packs/threshold-registry.yaml, the standalone threshold-contract SoT decided by epic #1200 D2 (standalone YAML registry: language-neutral, schema-validatable). STRICT at every level (additionalProperties:false) — this file is a hand-carried contract during the transition period, so a typo'd field or a mis-typed value must fail at author/CI time, not surface later as a silently-dropped threshold identity. Enforcement note: extraction is FULL (all packs/keys — mechanical), but the enforcement path this registry first serves is the 18-key repair line (#1196 / TRK-337). Validated BEFORE any generation stage by scripts/tools/lint/check_threshold_registry.py (pre-commit + CI).
$comment: Cross-entry constraints that JSON Schema cannot express — every keys.<k>.pack must exist under packs, every critical_of must name a key in the same pack, every deprecated_aliases target must name an existing key while its OLD spelling must NOT be an active key (both enforced fail-loud by build_registry_doc), and the whole document must stay semantically equal to scaffold_tenant.RULE_PACKS during the transition — are enforced by the equivalence assertion in check_threshold_registry.py (diff_vs_scaffold in _registry_lib.py). metric_class is an enum on purpose: adding a new class is a deliberate contract change and must touch this schema.

version.$comment: Registry FORMAT version (not the platform release). Bump only with a migration note in the file header.

deprecated_aliases.title: Retired threshold-key spellings still honored during their transition window (#1231)

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.$comment: old spelling -> canonical key. The old spelling stays pattern-legal (it WAS a key); the target must be an existing active key and the old spelling must not be — cross-checked fail-loud by build_registry_doc, not expressible here. This section is the alias SSOT: the Go (pkg/config/aliases.go deprecatedKeyAliases) and Python (_grar_validate.py DEPRECATED_KEY_ALIASES) runtime mirrors are pinned to it by tests.

deprecated_aliases.$comment: Optional and sparse: present only while at least one alias window is open. Authored in _registry_lib.DEPRECATED_KEY_ALIASES during the transition period (PR-3 folds it into the authored registry file).

packs.title: Pack-level metadata (one entry per rule pack, kubernetes included)

keys.title: Flat threshold-key identity map (the contract body)

pack.$comment: Must name an entry under packs (cross-checked by the gate, not expressible here).

tier.$comment: defaults = emitted by the platform-defaults path (reachable per TRK-337); optional_overrides = declared without a value — the platform recognises the key and asserts no number for it. WIRED as of #1310: the flat keys of this tier are shipped on the runtime `optional_overrides:` list (helm values + both onboarding `_defaults.yaml` producers), so a tenant sets one and resolveDeclaredRows emits it; `<base>_critical` keys stay off that list and resolve via resolveCriticalRows off defaults[base] instead. What the tier does NOT mean is 'not yet done' — an unset declared key is silent by design. Nor is the tier one population: of its 25 keys, the 9 flat ones are exactly the A-class of the 18 dead keys, while the other 16 are `<base>_critical` — and 5 of those are settable by a tenant TODAY because their base is a shipped chart default, so 'off the declared list' must never be read as 'dormant'. Which bucket a key lands in decides what a tenant can actually do with it, which is why tier is a load-bearing field, not decoration.

metric_class.description: Semantic class of the threshold key (REQUIRED on every key — #1200 WS1a PR-2). saturation = bounded-resource usage/backlog with a paired symptom metric (CURATED, product-facing: drives scaffold's educational _critical annotation + portal metricClass hints — membership changes are deliberate product decisions, not mechanical edits). capacity = fill level of a bounded space/allocation (disk, tablespace, log, parts, memory budget) without the paired-symptom curation. throughput = work-rate volume (qps, ops/s, req/s, msg/s). latency = time-to-complete or stall accumulation (GC pause, wait-time rate). replication = replica sync health (lag, under-replication, replication queue). state = discrete expected-value/topology invariant (cluster color, broker count, active controllers, consumers present). efficiency = cache/buffer effectiveness & waste (hit/miss ratio, evictions). errors = undesirable-event rate (deadlocks).
metric_class.$comment: _critical derivatives inherit the base key's class (build_registry_doc, never authored per-key). Adding a new class is a contract change: extend this enum deliberately and define it in the description.

chart_default.$comment: The Helm chart ships this key enabled (thresholdConfig.defaults + the dev conf.d template are GENERATED from this set — #1200 WS1a PR-2). Sparse: present iff true, like metric_class. Only meaningful on tier:defaults (build_registry_doc fails loudly otherwise). Widening the set (e.g. promoting pg_*) is a deliberate D4-family product decision, not a mechanical edit.

critical_of.$comment: DERIVED, never authored: present iff the key ends in _critical and its base key exists in the same pack. Names the base key.
